text.p: Following are the main stories in Swedish newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Goran Persson is getting more power, according to government critics. Former cabinet minister Anders Bjorck says the budget process has given the government more power and in turn increased Persson's influence.
- Sweden can expect a white Christmas and snowy New Year even though it is not forecast to be very cold with mild temperatures in the New year, according to the latest forecasts from SMHI.
- Traders have reported a three percent rise in sales this Christmas compared to a year ago with clothes and shoe sales particularly higher, says the Wholesale and Retail Organisation HUI.

- Slimming pills will be launched in Sweden next year, after approval from the EU Commission and are expected to get big sales. The pills contain dexenfluarmin and sibutramin which are appetite suppressants. In Sweden it is estimated six percent of men and 10 percent of women over the age of 16 are seriously overweight.
- Swedish telecommunications company Telia is threatened with damages for putting the wrong numbers for the employment office and regional social insurance office in the latest telephone directory.
